video_title: Guy Young on How to Build a 10 Times Better Product on Blockchain Rails
gist: Athena Labs founder Guy Young explains why he launched Athena Pay, a stablecoin-based neobank built on Avalanche, arguing DeFi TVL stagnation proves users won't come on-chain directly and that owning the USDe yield engine gives Athena a structural edge over neobanks that rely on Circle/Tether's stablecoins. He frames the $50-100B valuations of Tether/Circle/Binance as the template for what a 10x-better stablecoin neobank could become, while detailing USDe's track record, changed backing composition, and early Athena Pay adoption data.

insights.claim: DeFi TVL in the current cycle never broke its 2021 peak and was actually 30-40% below 2021 highs, which Athena's founder cites as the key data point proving that money is not migrating on-chain the way the industry expected.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A stalled DeFi TVL cycle vs. 2021 undercuts theses that assume secular on-chain user growth; treat DeFi as an infrastructure layer play, not a user-acquisition channel.
insights.quote: Looking at the data from this last cycle uh versus uh 2021 one D5 TVL actually didn't even break the peak of where we were in 2021 and it was actually you know 30 to 40% below the peaks

insights.claim: Guy Young believes DeFi's durable role is as backend infrastructure powering centralized, user-facing front ends (e.g., Morpho integrated into Coinbase and Robinhood) rather than as the destination where retail users directly interact via wallets and dApps.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Investors should value DeFi protocols on their embeddability as B2B2C infrastructure (integration deals with large fintechs/exchanges) rather than on direct-to-consumer wallet adoption metrics.

insights.claim: Athena applies a two-part test before entering a new product line: does it create a 10x better product for the end user, and does it create a 10x better business by rebuilding that product on crypto/stablecoin rails; both had to be a resounding yes before building Athena Pay.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A reusable screening framework for evaluating whether any traditional product category is ripe for a stablecoin-rail rebuild.
insights.quote: Does it produce like a 10 times better product for the user on the on the end? And then if you're successful in doing that, does it create like a 10 times better business rebuilding the stuff on crypto rails?

insights.claim: Guy Young sizes the stablecoin-neobank opportunity by analogy: stablecoins and exchanges have produced $50-100 billion outcomes (Binance, Coinbase, Tether, Circle), and comparable fintech neobanks like Revolut trade around a $100 billion valuation range, implying a rebuilt version on blockchain rails could reach similar scale.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Provides a rough valuation ceiling/comp set for any stablecoin-native neobank; useful anchor for private-market or pre-IPO valuation work on this category.
insights.quote: You look at a revolute in a new bank at a very similar sort of valuation range of hundred billion dollars and then you look at the actual product itself and just say you can do this better with rebuilding it on stable coin and blockchain rails.

insights.claim: Guy Young says this is the first time in his four to five years in crypto that a large addressable market (stablecoin neobanking) lacks an incumbent with the scale of Tether or Binance capable of crushing new entrants.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Signals a rare open competitive window in crypto-native consumer finance; worth tracking which teams move fastest before an incumbent (e.g., Tether/Plasma) consolidates share.

insights.claim: Guy Young does not view Plasma (a Tether-affiliated neobank he is personally invested in) as a competitor because he believes fighting over the existing 50,000-100,000 crypto-native app users is fighting for scraps compared to the real prize of onboarding 100 million+ non-crypto users.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Reframes the competitive set for stablecoin neobanks: the real race is against traditional fintech incumbents (Revolut, Chime-type apps) for mass-market users, not against other crypto-native apps.
insights.quote: Trying to compete over the 50 to 100,000 uh people who who are using the app right now kind of misses the bigger picture of like where this thing can go in an end state with new users

insights.claim: Existing crypto-native banking apps (including Athena Pay's likely early cohort) have only 100,000-150,000 total users combined, but their average revenue per user is roughly 10x that of a normal fintech user due to higher wealth and propensity to spend/save.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A small crypto-native user base can still be highly monetizable; ARPU, not just user count, is the metric to watch for early-stage crypto neobanks.
insights.quote: Even if you just look at the average revenue per users for some of the existing crypto banks versus normal fintex it's quite literally one order of magnitude larger.

insights.claim: Athena's go-to-market sequencing strategy is to first fully saturate its existing 100,000-150,000 crypto-native user base over a 6-9 month period before expanding Athena Pay to mainstream fintech users outside the crypto bubble.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Provides a timeline (roughly Q1-Q2 2027) after which Athena Pay's growth narrative should shift from crypto-native adoption metrics to mainstream fintech comparables.
insights.quote: I think we still have a six to nine month period to sort of fill out that first piece of the sequence that I was describing.

insights.claim: Guy Young says crypto users show low product loyalty and will switch neobank apps quickly for a better rate since migrating is as easy as sending a stablecoin to a new wallet, making the underlying yield engine the key defensible moat rather than brand or UX alone.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Churn risk is structurally high in crypto-native banking apps; investors should discount stickiness assumptions and focus on which player has the lowest-cost, highest, most sustainable yield source.
insights.quote: The crypto user is not that loyal at all... it's very easy for people to switch over which is quite literally sending one you know sending a stable coin from one wallet address to another.

insights.claim: Athena Pay balances are self-custodial stablecoin wallets by design but this is hidden from users via a 'name tag' contact system instead of wallet addresses and passkey/iCloud-based recovery instead of seed phrases, deliberately mimicking familiar fintech UX.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Illustrates a repeatable UX pattern (self-custody abstracted behind familiar auth) that other crypto consumer apps could copy to reduce onboarding friction.
insights.quote: It's actually pass key based with an email backup that sits behind it. So it essentially just follows you around with your iCloud uh iCloud account.

insights.claim: Because Athena Pay balances are self-custodial stablecoin wallets, the product can launch in ~50 countries on day one without needing new bank accounts, fiat rails, or regulatory licensing per country, a process that normally takes traditional fintechs 12-24 months per new market.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Self-custodial stablecoin architecture is a structural speed advantage for global expansion vs. licensed fintech competitors; a key differentiator to watch when comparing neobank rollout speed.
insights.quote: You kind of unlock the whole world just by default on day one because you know that doesn't require regulation and licensing to be able to offer a self-custodial stable coin wallet to users.

insights.claim: Athena Pay's card rollout speed is gated by third-party card infrastructure and issuance partners (compared by Guy Young to Rain, Reap, or Stripe-like providers) and by Visa's own country-by-country compliance requirements, and Guy Young notes market access has become harder over the past 18 months as local banks and payment companies, feeling threatened, push for more blocking of these products, a pressure he expects to continue.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Card-issuance infrastructure providers and incumbent-bank lobbying are the real chokepoints for stablecoin-neobank expansion speed, not Athena's own technology; watch for continued blocking pressure across the sector.
insights.quote: It wouldn't be you know surprising to me to see continued sort of pressure uh on blocking and the growth of these products going forward.

insights.claim: Guy Young argues that owning the yield-generating infrastructure (USDe) behind a neobank, rather than relying on Circle's or Tether's stablecoins, is a structural cost advantage because most competing neobanks bleed cash subsidizing savings incentives while Athena can fund free on-ramps and cashback from its own vertically integrated yield engine.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Vertical integration of stablecoin issuance + yield + consumer app captures NIM/float economics that would otherwise flow to Circle/Tether, a key differentiator vs. neobanks built on top of USDC/USDT.
insights.quote: The biggest beneficiaries of that weren't actually the NEO banks themselves. It was kind of circle and tether because all built on someone else's stable coin basically and they were able to monetize the NIM and uh the float.

insights.claim: sUSDe's lifetime average yield has been roughly 7%, above the current natural rate of about 4.75%; Athena Pay currently advertises a 6% savings rate and 5% cashback by subsidizing on top of the natural sUSDe yield during a bootstrap phase, and the subsidy will not last indefinitely.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Investors/users should not extrapolate the current 6%/5% promotional rates as permanent; expect convergence toward the underlying ~4.75-7% sUSDe range once subsidies are removed.
insights.quote: At the moment you're right, it's around 475 basis points for the natural SEO yield and uh in the app itself it's around six... that won't last indefinitely.

insights.claim: Guy Young contrasts Athena's structurally higher stablecoin yield against competing savings programs that merely layer temporary incentives on top of T-bill yields, arguing those programs 'always end up at T-bill yields' once the incentive is removed.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A useful heuristic for evaluating any stablecoin savings product: strip out promotional incentives and check what the durable base yield actually is versus T-bill benchmarks.
insights.quote: A lot of these other programs where you're just putting additional incentives on top of a T bill, it's always going to end up at T bill yields afterwards in the end.

insights.claim: Athena Pay's card is not a secured credit line against USDe with liquidation risk; instead, USDe backing is redeemed one step into USDC (or USDT/PYUSD) in the background to settle with Visa, since Visa only accepts USDC, USDT, and PYUSD as settlement currencies.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Clarifies there is no leverage/liquidation risk in Athena Pay card spending, an important risk-management distinction for users and analysts modeling counterparty risk.
insights.quote: There's no kind of uh lending or leverage against USD in the process.

insights.claim: Guy Young considers card interchange and FX fee revenue the most strategically valuable new revenue stream from Athena Pay because it is uncorrelated to USDe's NIM/interest generation, diversifying Athena away from pure dependence on the crypto price cycle.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A blueprint for crypto-native fintechs to build cycle-resistant revenue: pair crypto-native yield products with fee-based, spend-driven revenue lines uncorrelated to token prices.

insights.claim: Athena now operates three business lines: USDe (described as the second-largest on-chain savings product), a white-label stablecoin-issuance business (described as the largest in the space), and Athena Pay, which the founder sees as synergistic since Athena Pay is a distribution channel for USDe while USDe funds Athena Pay's yield.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Athena's white-label stablecoin-issuance business being the largest in its category is a notable, possibly underappreciated revenue line beyond USDe itself worth independent diligence.

themes.theme: USDe Backing, Risk Profile & Track Record

insights.claim: USDe has processed approximately $30 billion in cumulative mint and redemption flows, with supply peaking around $15 billion, and survived both the Binance '10/10' deleveraging event in late 2025 and an Aave-related incident in Q2 2025 without losing users any money.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A concrete stress-test track record for USDe across two major market dislocations; useful evidence when underwriting USDe's peg/redemption reliability versus other synthetic dollar products.
insights.quote: There's been around like $30 billion of mint and redemption flows within USD peaked at around $15 billion and then we went through the Binance uh 1010 you know deleveraging event... and nothing did go wrong.

insights.claim: USDe's backing composition has shifted so that the original basis trade now makes up only about 10% of collateral, with the remainder in institutional lending and collateralized loan obligations (CLOs), which Guy Young argues makes the product safer, not riskier, than its original structure.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A material change in USDe's risk composition that any USDe holder or counterparty should re-underwrite; basis-trade/exchange counterparty risk has fallen but institutional lending/CLO credit risk has risen as a share of backing.
insights.quote: PERBs are about a tenth of the backing and then the rest is um institutional lending, collateralized loan ob obligations... the composition of what we do within USD I would actually argue has become like safer through time.

insights.claim: Guy Young explicitly acknowledges there is real risk of losing money in USDe despite its clean track record, declining to guarantee future performance ('you can never say never'), and notes that Athena has at various points been one of the largest holders of Tether, Circle, and PayPal USD (PYUSD) reserves as part of USDe's backing since Visa's card network only settles in USDC, USDT, and PYUSD.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A direct risk disclosure plus a concentration point: USDe holders bear both general product risk and indirect exposure to Tether/Circle/PayPal stablecoin redemption reliability.
insights.quote: There is definitely a risk that like uh you can lose money on USD... you can never say never sort of going forward.

insights.claim: Guy Young argues the entire KYC regulatory regime needs a fundamental rethink, questioning whether collecting home addresses (versus just country verification) is necessary given the near-weekly data breach incidents like the Revolut hack, in which an attacker posing as a government agency obtained customer passports, selfies, and transaction histories.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A pointed critique from a fintech founder that KYC over-collection is creating physical-safety risk for users; relevant to ongoing regulatory debates about data minimization in financial KYC.
insights.quote: Does the benefits of, you know, uh, forcing this into every financial interaction everyone has in their lives actually make sense relative to like the mounting cost that we're seeing with like almost a weekly incident like this happening.

insights.claim: Athena Pay outsources KYC and compliance entirely to Sumsub and Rain rather than building an in-house compliance team, on the reasoning that specialized providers serving larger businesses do it more securely than Athena could on its own.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Signals which compliance infrastructure vendors (Sumsub, Rain) are becoming default picks for crypto-native neobanks; a distribution/dependency data point for those vendors' growth.

insights.claim: Guy Young states that Athena Pay's KYC requirements are dictated downstream by Visa's and its card-issuer partners' compliance rules, not by Athena's own policy choice, even though he personally disagrees with the current level of KYC data collection.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Visa's compliance requirements effectively set the KYC floor for the entire stablecoin-card industry, meaning reform would need to happen at the card-network level, not at individual issuers.
insights.quote: This isn't necessarily like a decision that's sitting with us... it's really just us providing a level that's required of uh our users before they're actually able to use the products that uh rely on on uh Visa payments.

insights.claim: Two weeks after launch, Athena Pay has a waitlist of 10,000-15,000 people but has only admitted about 400 users in a deliberately controlled, gated beta rollout, with most early adopters concentrated in South America and Asia and some being pre-existing USDe holders.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Very early, small-sample adoption data; useful baseline for tracking Athena Pay's growth trajectory in subsequent quarters, and confirms South America/Asia (not the US) as the initial beachhead.

insights.claim: Guy Young was surprised that some early Athena Pay users deposited one to two million dollars within five minutes of the app's first-day launch, a level of trust he says exceeded his own confidence in the untested new mobile app after a month of personal use.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Anecdotal but notable evidence of high-conviction capital willing to move quickly into a brand-new stablecoin neobank app, suggesting strong trust carryover from Athena's existing USDe user base.
insights.quote: A few guys throwing in like one or two million dollars on like the first day of the launch into this like new mobile app that they've never used before and it was like within 5 minutes.

insights.claim: Despite the US being the largest and one of the richest consumer markets globally, Guy Young says the US is not even a top-five priority market for Athena Pay; the company's historical data shows South America and Asia are the strongest-demand regions, mirroring how Tether built its dominance offshore rather than in developed markets with existing good financial infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Investors modeling stablecoin-neobank TAM should weight emerging-market dollar demand over developed-market opportunity, following the Tether playbook rather than a US-first fintech strategy.
insights.quote: I wouldn't say the US is our biggest target market um at all... it was really South America and Asia which drove a lot of the growth uh for us.

insights.claim: Athena Pay chose Avalanche (rather than Ethereum, despite Athena's name deriving from ETH) as its settlement backend for USDe transfers because Avalanche has positioned itself as backend infrastructure for real businesses serving users outside crypto, an alignment Guy Young says other chains lack due to being generalized or trading/derivatives-focused.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Signals that chain selection for consumer fintech apps is increasingly driven by brand/positioning fit (real-world business infrastructure) rather than technical differentiation alone; relevant to Avalanche's competitive narrative versus other L1s.
insights.quote: Avalanche I think is always come out with the um you know pretty consistent line of this is backend infrastructure for just real businesses uh that are operating and serving users outside of uh the space.

insights.claim: Athena Pay's cashback rewards are paid exclusively in AVAX, funded directly by the Avalanche team, an arrangement Guy Young expects to continue for at least the next couple of years but does not guarantee will last indefinitely, noting that similar card reward programs have historically swapped between native tokens, ETH, and USDC over time.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: AVAX-funded cashback represents a direct token-level marketing spend by the Avalanche Foundation/team to drive Athena Pay adoption; a partnership economics detail relevant to AVAX token demand modeling.
insights.quote: It is exclusive on Avalanche uh in terms of Athena Pay and um yeah I'd say base expectations is the next couple of years at least um we're expecting that the the rewards will be paid in in AEX.

insights.claim: Guy Young says he never times product launches or roadmap decisions around perceived crypto market cycles, viewing quiet, low-distraction bear-market periods (like 2023, when Athena itself was founded) as the best time to build because there is less market noise for the team.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: A founder-level counter-signal against consensus market-timing behavior: building through bear markets when competitors and talent are distracted by price action can be a structural advantage.
insights.quote: This is actually kind of the absolute best time to build things which is the market is less distracting... you can actually just focus on the only thing that actually matters which is building a good product.

insights.claim: Guy Young holds a low-confidence view that the crypto bear market's worst point has likely passed, attributing the unusual severity of investor pain this cycle to the absence of a single identifiable blowup (unlike Luna or FTX in 2022) combined with a stark divergence where crypto fell roughly 80% while AI stocks and gold each roughly doubled multiple times over the same period, but now sees 'green shoots' of relative-value optimism emerging.
insights.speaker: Guy Young
insights.so_what: Frames current crypto valuations as cheap on a relative-value basis versus other risk assets (AI equities, gold), a possible tactical entry thesis, though the speaker flags his own track record of being wrong on market calls.
insights.quote: You're just watching like AI go up 10x, gold go up 10x, and then um, you know, uh, crypto down 80% over the same time period... on a relative value basis, this is all like quite cheap.
